requirements.requirement: curl package is held at its current installed version (8.12.1-4.el10) on node1 so future updates do not change it
requirements.summary: Baseline curl version 8.12.1-4.el10 was identified, the dnf versionlock plugin was installed, and a versionlock entry for curl-0:8.12.1-4.el10.* was added and confirmed present via `dnf versionlock list`.

requirements.requirement: A system update leaves curl excluded/unchanged (verification that the hold actually works)
requirements.summary: A dry-run `dnf upgrade --assumeno` enumerated 250 packages including libcurl (a separate package) but no curl entry, and a targeted grep for curl/versionlock/excluding lines in the plan returned nothing, directly demonstrating curl was excluded from the pending update set.

requirements.requirement: Version-lock hold persists across a restart / system state remains healthy
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (boot_id deef5424..., curl version, versionlock entry) was captured, the node was rebooted, boot_id changed to 77ffbf46... confirming an actual restart, and post-restart checks show curl version and versionlock entry unchanged plus `systemctl is-system-running` reporting 'running'. This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots showing matching boot-identity change and no failed services after executor.

overall_summary: The executor correctly locked curl at its installed version using dnf versionlock, empirically verified via a dry-run upgrade that curl is excluded from a pending system update, and separately completed the mandated node-restart evidence protocol showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery with the version lock intact and the system reporting healthy. All observed state changes are directly tied to the task or the restart protocol, with only a trivial log file left as an expected byproduct.
limitations: No independent confirmation that the versionlock configuration file on disk (e.g. /etc/dnf/plugins/versionlock.conf) was inspected directly; evidence relies on `dnf versionlock list` output rather than the raw config file.

The falsification check used --assumeno so no real update was ever applied; behavior under an actual completed update was not observed, though this is a reasonable and standard way to verify a hold without mutating the system unnecessarily.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (installing the versionlock plugin, adding the versionlock entry, the dry-run upgrade probe, and the mandated reboot) map directly to satisfying the task or the required restart-evidence protocol; the dry-run upgrade used --assumeno so it made no package changes despite listing 250 candidates. The only incidental artifact is /tmp/reboot.log, a redirect target created by the backgrounded `shutdown -r now` command used to return an acknowledgement before disconnect (cmd-28d0aa5740c34550); it is a small, expected byproduct of a mandated low-risk restart action rather than unbounded residue, and no other unnecessary mutations, failed services, or exposure changes were introduced (listening sockets and package-health are equivalent before/after, only ephemeral PIDs differ).
